messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Converting DArT data to COANCESTORY format
parts:
Hi,

 

I was just toying again with ways to get relatedness into dartR (as quite some people are requesting it).

 

Here is an approach that did not work some time ago as the package relatedness seemed not to work reliably with a greater number of SNPs. Seems to be better now. So in case someone wants to test this here is the way to do it:

 

  1. Install package related “by hand”.
  2. Replace the line x<- bandicoot.gl  with x <- yourgenlight object
  3. Run the rest of the script and modify the coancestry part, if you want to have different estimates

 

In case you want to export to run the gui, you should be able to uncomment the write.table command below. [I have not tested it to run with coancestry yet].

 

In case it works please let me know, then I will add a function to dartR.

 

 

Relatedness is a package that wraps around the fortran code of coancestry so should have identical results. If some can check that would be great.

 

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

 

 

#install.packages("related", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

library(related)

 

 

x <- bandicoot.gl[1:10,]#[1:10,1:7]

gd <- as.matrix(x)

 

mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=nrow(gd), ncol =ncol(gd)*2 )

mm[, seq(1,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,0,mm)

 

mm[, seq(2,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,2,mm)

 

mm <- mm+1

mm <- ifelse(is.na(mm),0,mm)

 

gtd <- data.frame(V1=as.character(indNames(x)), mm)

gtd$V1 <- as.character(gtd$V1)

 

#export as file

#write.table(gtd, file = "gtd.txt", sep = "\t",col.names = F, row.names = F)

#load from file

#gtd <- readgenotypedata("gtd.txt")$gdata

 

#---Calculate Relatedness---#

output <- coancestry(gtd, lynchrd=2, quellergt=2, wang=2)

 

#---View Point Estimates---#

output$relatedness

On Tuesday, November 26, 2019 at 1:37:27 PM UTC+10:30, Bernd. Gruber wrote:

Hi,

 

I was just toying again with ways to get relatedness into dartR (as quite some people are requesting it).

 

Here is an approach that did not work some time ago as the package relatedness seemed not to work reliably with a greater number of SNPs. Seems to be better now. So in case someone wants to test this here is the way to do it:

 

  1. Install package related “by hand”.
  2. Replace the line x<- bandicoot.gl  with x <- yourgenlight object
  3. Run the rest of the script and modify the coancestry part, if you want to have different estimates

 

In case you want to export to run the gui, you should be able to uncomment the write.table command below. [I have not tested it to run with coancestry yet].

 

In case it works please let me know, then I will add a function to dartR.

 

 

Relatedness is a package that wraps around the fortran code of coancestry so should have identical results. If some can check that would be great.

 

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

 

 

#install.packages("related", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

library(related)

 

 

x <- bandicoot.gl[1:10,]#[1:10,1:7]

gd <- as.matrix(x)

 

mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=nrow(gd), ncol =ncol(gd)*2 )

mm[, seq(1,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,0,mm)

 

mm[, seq(2,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,2,mm)

 

mm <- mm+1

mm <- ifelse(is.na(mm),0,mm)

 

gtd <- data.frame(V1=as.character(indNames(x)), mm)

gtd$V1 <- as.character(gtd$V1)

 

#export as file

#write.table(gtd, file = "gtd.txt", sep = "\t",col.names = F, row.names = F)

#load from file

#gtd <- readgenotypedata("gtd.txt")$gdata

 

#---Calculate Relatedness---#

output <- coancestry(gtd, lynchrd=2, quellergt=2, wang=2)

 

#---View Point Estimates---#

output$relatedness

Hi Bernd,
Just following up on this post in case it is useful to you or anyone else reading.
I found this 2018 paper to be helpful: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/29160928
The authors mention a pers. comm from the author of the RELATED r package who says that it is not able to deal with large SNP data sets. This may explain why my R console was left hanging when I tried to obtain relatedness estimates from my full dataset of 395 loci with 100+ individuals. 
I have since run the Coancestry GUI on a similar sized dataset and everything seems to be working.
As for my earlier issue with obtaining a relatedness value of more than 1, I have since read that this happens in the case of haplodiploidy, so at least this is not a technical issue. I am going to try the software PolyRelatedness (Huang 2014) as an alternative for this nematode dataset. 
cheers,
Bonnie

On Wednesday, December 4, 2019 at 11:44:00 AM UTC+8, Bonnie D wrote:
Hi Bernd,

I've just tried the gtd object in the Coancestry GUI. The subset of 10 individuals and 395 loci ran ok, though for some reason the Wang's estimates are different to when the data are run in the related pkg - I will look further into the parameters. 

When uploading the text file, the GUI does warn that only the first 101 columns will be displayed- though I checked with a reduced dataset of 100 loci and the first run does indeed analyse all the loci.

I still do get a value of over 1 for one dyad containing the same problem individual. I will try some more reading and googling.

Cheers,
Bonnie


On Tuesday, December 3, 2019 at 2:36:29 PM UTC+10:30, Bernd. Gruber wrote:

Hi Bonnie,

 

Thanks for letting me know. That is good. Can you by any chance have a run of  your data with the coancestry programme and check if you have the same issue. I ran into problems when I ran the coancestry gui with that many SNPS, but when I ran the command line version I got the exactly same result.

 

Thanks and cheers ,Bernd

Hi Bernd,

I gave your code a go for converting my genlight object (nematode with 395 loci, 3.17% missing data) into a format useable by the package related. As far as I can tell it works well. 

 

The only strange thing about my results is Wang's estimate results in values of -1.x when a certain individual is part of the dyad. Looking at the gtd matrix doesn't provide any clues as to what is different about this individual. Anyway, I am assuming that this is a problem with my data and not the conversion.

 

Thanks for the handy code.

Cheers,

Bonnie

 

 

 

On Tuesday, November 26, 2019 at 1:37:27 PM UTC+10:30, Bernd. Gruber wrote:

Hi,

 

I was just toying again with ways to get relatedness into dartR (as quite some people are requesting it).

 

Here is an approach that did not work some time ago as the package relatedness seemed not to work reliably with a greater number of SNPs. Seems to be better now. So in case someone wants to test this here is the way to do it:

 

  1. Install package related “by hand”.
  2. Replace the line x<- bandicoot.gl  with x <- yourgenlight object
  3. Run the rest of the script and modify the coancestry part, if you want to have different estimates

 

In case you want to export to run the gui, you should be able to uncomment the write.table command below. [I have not tested it to run with coancestry yet].

 

In case it works please let me know, then I will add a function to dartR.

 

 

Relatedness is a package that wraps around the fortran code of coancestry so should have identical results. If some can check that would be great.

 

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

 

 

#install.packages("related", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

library(related)

 

 

x <- bandicoot.gl[1:10,]#[1:10,1:7]

gd <- as.matrix(x)

 

mm <- matrix(NA, nrow=nrow(gd), ncol =ncol(gd)*2 )

mm[, seq(1,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,0,mm)

 

mm[, seq(2,nLoc(x)*2,2)] <- gd

mm <- ifelse(mm==1,2,mm)

 

mm <- mm+1

mm <- ifelse(is.na(mm),0,mm)

 

gtd <- data.frame(V1=as.character(indNames(x)), mm)

gtd$V1 <- as.character(gtd$V1)

 

#export as file

#write.table(gtd, file = "gtd.txt", sep = "\t",col.names = F, row.names = F)

#load from file

#gtd <- readgenotypedata("gtd.txt")$gdata

 

#---Calculate Relatedness---#

output <- coancestry(gtd, lynchrd=2, quellergt=2, wang=2)

 

#---View Point Estimates---#

output$relatedness
